interest: U.S. intelligence on Japanese forces in Shanghai and Nisei in Hawaii.
overview: This State Department decimal file (894.22/24 through 894.22/26), spanning October 1940 to January 1942, documents U.S. military and diplomatic surveillance of Japanese military personnel, organization, and overseas postings under the classification for personnel, organization, discipline, mutiny, and compulsory military service. The file consists of three main records: an October 1940 transmittal letter from the Secretary of the Navy conveying a Fourteenth Naval District report on second-generation Japanese reaching military age in Hawaii; an extensive October 1941 Office of Naval Intelligence report by U.S. Marine Corps Major G. W. Williams detailing Japanese Army and Navy headquarters, garrison units, liaison officers, gendarmerie, and fleet commanders stationed in Shanghai; and a January 1942 War Department cross-reference sheet monitoring Japanese military attachés in Bolivia, Peru, and Chile shortly after the outbreak of war.
